research_question: What is the effect of ultrasound-guided erector spinae plane block (ESPB), compared with no block, on cumulative postoperative opioid consumption at 24 hours in adults undergoing surgery?
control_label: no block (general anaesthesia and usual analgesia only, no injection)
outcome_description: cumulative postoperative opioid consumption over the first 24 hours after surgery (in milligrams of oral morphine equivalents)
positive_direction: ESPB reduces 24-hour cumulative postoperative opioid consumption compared to no block (lower opioid use in ESPB group)
search_queries: erector spinae plane block postoperative opioid consumption trial
erector spinae block postoperative morphine trial
ESPB randomized controlled trial opioid consumption
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trials evaluating ultrasound-guided erector spinae plane block (ESPB) versus a no-block control in adult surgical patients
Reports cumulative postoperative opioid consumption over the first 24 hours post-surgery
Provides quantitative outcome data convertible to oral morphine equivalents in milligrams with measures of central tendency and dispersion
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, conference abstracts without full data, editorials, commentaries, case reports, or study protocols)
No comparison between ESPB and a true no-block control group (e.g., trials with sham/saline injection control, or active comparison with other regional blocks/epidurals)
No quantitative 24-hour cumulative postoperative opioid consumption data that can produce an effect size (means/SDs or convertible medians/IQRs)
Studies conducted in pediatric populations (<18 years of age) or non-surgical/chronic pain settings
moderators_to_extract: Type of surgical procedure (e.g., thoracic, abdominal, spinal, breast, laparoscopic)
ESPB technique and regimen (single-shot vs. continuous catheter; local anesthetic type, concentration, and volume)
Timing of block administration (preoperative vs. postoperative)
Primary postoperative PCA opioid regimen and delivery route
effect_size_note: Pool as mean difference (MD) in milligrams of oral morphine equivalents (OME). All opioids must be converted to oral morphine equivalents using standard equianalgesic conversion factors. When median and IQR are reported, estimate mean and SD using standard methods (e.g., Wan et al. or Hozo et al.). If SE or SEM is reported, convert to SD = SE * sqrt(n). An MD < 0 indicates lower opioid consumption in the ESPB group.
